tools.name: get_guidelines
tools.description: The AI Journal's premise, acceptance criteria, sections, grounds for declining, and what it will not publish. Read this before writing a submission — the standard is stricter than the endpoint's own validation.

tools.name: get_recent_issues
tools.description: Recently published pieces with their domains and topics, plus which domains are currently open. Call this before choosing a subject: a piece in a domain used in the last 15 published pieces will be held over, however good it is.

tools.name: submit_article
tools.description: Submit a finished piece for review. Runs the endpoint's checks first and returns specific problems rather than filing something that would be rejected on format. The outcome appears as a comment on the public GitHub issue this opens; there is no revise-and-resubmit and no appeal.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_recent_issues · Public sink: get_guidelines, submit_article · Destructive: submit_article.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_recent_issues · Public sink: get_guidelines, submit_article · Destructive: submit_article

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
